titleEn: As Soft as a Marmot's Voice!

pages.text: "Marmot! Come oooout!" Leo the know-it-all fox lifted his muzzle and shouted at a burrow. His voice rang across the slope. The marmot at the entrance slipped inside.
"I call the best, so I'll see one first!" Leo wanted to see a marmot right up close. Mei the timid baby goat stood quietly behind.
Leo shouted at the next burrow too. "Marmot here! I said, come out!" The grass grew quiet. Not a marmot showed at any burrow.
The sun was high. All marmot sounds on the slope had stopped. Leo lay in front of a burrow and peered in. Dark, and nothing to see.
Mei said softly, "Maybe your voice is too loud, Leo." "What's wrong with my voice?" he answered loudly again. At that sound, even the burrows below grew quiet.
Grandma Bear lay beside Leo and peered in too. Then she put a finger to her lips. Shh. Far away came a tiny whistle.
"Heard that? Marmots speak that softly," Grandma whispered. Leo tried lowering his voice. "Marmot... As soft as a marmot's voice!"
Grass rustled. A marmot popped out before the burrow. With ears perked, it stared at Leo. Leo held his breath and stayed still.
Leo whispered in Mei's ear. "One, whisper by a burrow! Two, as soft as a marmot's voice! Three, far away, we can be loud!" Two marmots came out, then three.
Grandma hugged Leo close to her side as they watched the burrow. With a softer voice, the marmots came out first. Leo whispered, "As soft as a marmot's voice!"
